# Sightline

> Sightline is a free, open-source (MIT) tool that draws a live map of C#, TypeScript and JavaScript code in the browser. It reads each language with its own compiler (C# with Roslyn, TypeScript and JavaScript with the TypeScript compiler) and shows projects and their NuGet and npm packages, namespaces, folders and types, dependency injection registrations and their lifetimes (and NestJS providers), HTTP endpoints, and the path each request takes through handlers, services and repositories down to the database and outbound HTTP calls. An HTTP call that fits an endpoint on the map leads into it, also from one language into another, such as a React client calling an ASP.NET Core API. The map updates while you edit the code. Latest version: {{version}}.

- Try it without installing anything: run `dnx Co.Revington.Sightline` in a folder with a `.sln` or a `package.json`. It is installed with .NET whatever the language of the code, so it needs the .NET 10 SDK or newer, and Node.js 18 or newer to read TypeScript and JavaScript. The map opens in the browser, by default at `http://localhost:5210`.
- Endpoints it reads: ASP.NET Core controllers and minimal APIs, SignalR hubs, gRPC services and health checks; Express (and routers like it), Fastify, Koa, Hono, NestJS and Next.js route handlers.
- Set it up for a team: `dnx Co.Revington.Sightline init` pins the tool in `dotnet-tools.json` and writes `sightline.json`. Teammates then run `dotnet tool restore` once, and `dotnet sightline`.
- Commands: `sightline [path]` opens the map. `sightline check` lists problems and exits with 1 when there are errors, for CI. `sightline export --out <dir>` writes the map as a static website. `sightline diff --base <ref>` shows what a change does to the map. `sightline mcp` serves the map to AI assistants over the Model Context Protocol.
- Problems it finds as you type: a singleton that holds a scoped service (a captive dependency), a service nobody registered, services that need each other, a project that breaks the layer rules in `sightline.json`, and registrations nothing asks for. In NestJS code: providers no module provides, providers that need each other, and providers nothing injects.
- The `Co.Revington.Sightline.Hosting` package opens the map beside a .NET app on every Debug run, and adds what the running app does: its real registrations and endpoints, each request with its SQL and outbound HTTP calls, and "Try it" on each endpoint. Release builds get nothing from it.
- Also: a VS Code extension, a GitHub Action that comments on pull requests, and tours that walk a new teammate through the code.
- Limits: C# (SDK-style projects), TypeScript and JavaScript; other languages are not read yet. Reading C# does not follow reflection, assembly scanning or generated code; with the Hosting package, the running app fills those gaps for registrations and endpoints. In JavaScript and TypeScript, GraphQL, tRPC, WebSocket and message handlers are not followed, and running Node.js apps do not report to the map.
- Privacy: it runs on your machine and sends nothing anywhere.

## Docs

- [Full documentation](https://sightline.revington.co/llms-full.txt): the README as Markdown: commands and options, checks, settings, the running app, the views, editing, exported maps, limits and safety
- [Hosting package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ravindu-rev/sightline/master/src/Co.Revington.Sightline.Hosting/README.md): how `Co.Revington.Sightline.Hosting` behaves in an app
- [VS Code extension](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ravindu-rev/sightline/master/vscode/README.md): the extension's commands and settings
- [Settings schema](https://sightline.revington.co/sightline.schema.json): JSON schema for `sightline.json`

## Packages and source

- [Co.Revington.Sightline on NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Co.Revington.Sightline): the tool, which is also an MCP server package
- [Co.Revington.Sightline.Hosting on NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Co.Revington.Sightline.Hosting): starts the map beside your .NET app
- [VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=revington.sightline)
- [GitHub Action](https://github.com/ravindu-rev/sightline-action): comments on each pull request with what it changes on the map
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/ravindu-rev/sightline)
- [Release notes](https://github.com/ravindu-rev/sightline/releases)

## Optional

- [Live demo](https://sightline.revington.co/demo/): the real interface, running in the browser on a recording of the C# sample shop; needs JavaScript
- [Map of dotnet/eShop](https://sightline.revington.co/explore/eshop/): Sightline's exported map of a 28-project open-source .NET solution; needs JavaScript
